items.name: Developmental psychology
items.plain_en: study of behavior and thought changes across lifespan

items.name: Nature versus nurture
items.plain_en: heredity versus environment as influences on development

items.name: Cross-sectional research
items.plain_en: compares different ages at one point in time

items.name: Longitudinal research
items.plain_en: follows one group of participants over time

items.name: Genetics
items.plain_en: genes shape inborn abilities and motor development

items.name: Teratogens
items.plain_en: chemicals or agents that can harm fetus

items.name: Fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS)
items.plain_en: severe developmental disorder from heavy prenatal alcohol

items.name: Fetal alcohol effect
items.plain_en: milder effect of moderate drinking during pregnancy

items.name: Reflexes
items.plain_en: inborn automatic responses to specific stimuli

items.name: Rooting reflex
items.plain_en: baby turns head toward cheek touch

items.name: Sucking reflex
items.plain_en: infant sucks objects placed in mouth

items.name: Grasping reflex
items.plain_en: baby grasps objects touching palm or foot

items.name: Moro reflex
items.plain_en: startled baby flings out then retracts limbs

items.name: Babinski reflex
items.plain_en: stroked foot makes baby spread toes

items.name: Visual cliff
items.plain_en: apparatus testing infant depth perception

items.name: Motor development
items.plain_en: motor skills develop in same sequence

items.name: Gender roles
items.plain_en: behaviors a culture associates with each gender

items.name: Biopsychological (Neuropsychological) Theory
items.plain_en: biological factors explain gender role development

items.name: Social-Cognitive Theory
items.plain_en: society and thoughts shape gender roles

items.name: Gender schema theory
items.plain_en: internal interpretations of environmental gender messages

items.name: Stage theories
items.plain_en: development occurs in distinct discontinuous stages

items.name: Zone of proximal development
items.plain_en: tasks child can do alone versus with help

items.name: Psychosocial stage theory
items.plain_en: eight stages each centered on social conflict

items.name: Autonomy
items.plain_en: control over one's own body

items.name: Inferiority complex
items.plain_en: feeling inadequate compared with peers

items.name: Imaginary audience
items.plain_en: adolescents believe others constantly watch them

items.name: Schemata
items.plain_en: cognitive rules used to interpret world

items.name: Assimilation
items.plain_en: fitting new experiences into existing schemata

items.name: Accommodation
items.plain_en: changing schemata when new information does not fit

items.name: Object permanence
items.plain_en: objects continue existing when out of sight

items.name: Egocentric
items.plain_en: unable to see another person's perspective

items.name: Theory of mind
items.plain_en: ability to consider others' mental states

items.name: Conservation
items.plain_en: properties stay same despite changes in shape

items.name: Abstract reasoning
items.plain_en: manipulating ideas mentally without concrete objects

items.name: Metacognition
items.plain_en: thinking about one's own thinking

items.name: Personal fable
items.plain_en: belief in own uniqueness and invulnerability

items.name: Information processing model
items.plain_en: cognitive abilities develop gradually with age

items.name: Phonemes
items.plain_en: smallest units of sound in language

items.name: Morpheme
items.plain_en: smallest meaningful unit of sound

items.name: Syntax
items.plain_en: rules for ordering words in sentences

items.name: Semantics
items.plain_en: meanings of words and sentences

items.name: Babbling stage
items.plain_en: first language stage beginning around four months

items.name: Holophrases
items.plain_en: one-word stage of language acquisition

items.name: Telegraphic speech
items.plain_en: two-word stage beginning around eighteen months

items.name: Overgeneralization
items.plain_en: misapplying grammar rules to new cases

items.name: Language acquisition device
items.plain_en: inborn ability to learn language rapidly

items.name: Critical period
items.plain_en: limited window when a skill must develop

items.name: Linguistic relativity hypothesis
items.plain_en: language controls and limits our thinking

items.name: Attachment parenting
items.plain_en: reciprocal relationship between caregiver and child

items.name: Imprinting
items.plain_en: infant animals attach to first seen object

items.name: Contact comfort
items.plain_en: physical comfort fosters attachment to parents

items.name: Temperament
items.plain_en: typical emotional style of reacting to stress

items.name: Secure attachment
items.plain_en: explores confidently but distressed by parent leaving

items.name: Avoidant attachment
items.plain_en: resists being held, avoids parent contact

items.name: Anxious/ambivalent attachment
items.plain_en: ambivalent anxious reactions toward the parent

items.name: Ecological systems theory
items.plain_en: development shaped by nested environmental relationship systems

items.name: Microsystem
items.plain_en: child's direct interactions with immediate surroundings

items.name: Mesosystem
items.plain_en: interactions among the five ecological systems

items.name: Exosystem
items.plain_en: indirect environmental influences on child development

items.name: Macrosystem
items.plain_en: cultural influences on a child's development

items.name: Chronosystem
items.plain_en: timing of transitions across child's life

items.name: Authoritarian parents
items.plain_en: strict standards enforced through punishment

items.name: Permissive parents
items.plain_en: few or unclear guidelines for children

items.name: Authoritative parents
items.plain_en: consistent reasonable standards explained to children

items.name: Learning
items.plain_en: lasting behavior change caused by experience

items.name: Classical conditioning
items.plain_en: neutral stimulus paired with reflexive response

items.name: Unconditioned stimulus (US or UCS)
items.plain_en: stimulus naturally eliciting an unlearned response

items.name: Unconditioned response (UR or UCR)
items.plain_en: natural involuntary response to unconditioned stimulus

items.name: Conditioned stimulus (CS)
items.plain_en: previously neutral stimulus that now elicits response

items.name: Conditioned response (CR)
items.plain_en: learned response to conditioned stimulus

items.name: Acquisition
items.plain_en: learning a new conditioned response

items.name: Delayed conditioning
items.plain_en: CS presented before US while still present

items.name: Trace conditioning
items.plain_en: CS then pause then US

items.name: Simultaneous conditioning
items.plain_en: CS and US presented together

items.name: Backward conditioning
items.plain_en: US presented before the CS

items.name: Extinction
items.plain_en: weakening and unlearning a conditioned response

items.name: Spontaneous recovery
items.plain_en: extinguished response briefly returns after conditioned stimulus

items.name: Generalization
items.plain_en: responding to similar conditioned stimuli

items.name: Discrimination
items.plain_en: learning to distinguish among similar stimuli

items.name: Aversive conditioning
items.plain_en: pairing neutral stimulus with unpleasant response

items.name: Higher-order conditioning
items.plain_en: using conditioned stimulus to condition new one

items.name: Taste aversion
items.plain_en: aversion to food after nausea

items.name: Biological preparedness
items.plain_en: biological predisposition to learn certain associations

items.name: Salient stimuli
items.plain_en: noticeable stimuli produce stronger conditioned responses

items.name: Garcia effect
items.plain_en: animals easily learn taste aversions

items.name: Operant conditioning
items.plain_en: learning based on consequences of behavior

items.name: Law of effect
items.plain_en: pleasant consequences strengthen stimulus-response connection

items.name: Instrumental learning
items.plain_en: consequences shape future behaviors

items.name: Reinforcer
items.plain_en: anything making behavior more likely

items.name: Positive reinforcement
items.plain_en: adding pleasant stimulus strengthens behavior

items.name: Negative reinforcement
items.plain_en: removing unpleasant stimulus strengthens behavior

items.name: Escape learning
items.plain_en: learning to terminate aversive stimulus

items.name: Avoidance learning
items.plain_en: learning to prevent unpleasant stimulus entirely

items.name: Punishment
items.plain_en: anything making behavior less likely

items.name: Positive punishment
items.plain_en: adding unpleasant stimulus reduces behavior

items.name: Omission training
items.plain_en: removing pleasant stimulus reduces behavior

items.name: Shaping
items.plain_en: reinforcing steps toward desired behavior

items.name: Chaining
items.plain_en: linking successive responses for a reward

items.name: Discriminative stimulus
items.plain_en: signal indicating reinforcement is available

items.name: Primary reinforcers
items.plain_en: reinforcers rewarding in themselves

items.name: Secondary reinforcers
items.plain_en: learned reinforcers such as praise

items.name: Generalized reinforcer
items.plain_en: secondary reinforcer exchangeable for many things

items.name: Token economy
items.plain_en: tokens earned for desired behaviors

items.name: Premack principle
items.plain_en: preferred activity reinforces less preferred activity

items.name: Continuous reinforcement
items.plain_en: rewarding every target behavior

items.name: Partial-reinforcement effect
items.plain_en: intermittent reinforcement makes extinction harder

items.name: Fixed-ratio (FR) schedule
items.plain_en: reinforcement after set number of responses

items.name: Variable-ratio (VR) schedule
items.plain_en: reinforcement after varying number of responses

items.name: Fixed-interval (FI) schedule
items.plain_en: reinforcement after fixed time interval

items.name: Variable-interval (VI) schedule
items.plain_en: reinforcement after varying time intervals

items.name: Instinctive drift
items.plain_en: animals revert to instinctive behavior over rewards

items.name: Contiguity model
items.plain_en: more pairings produce stronger learning

items.name: Contingency model of classical conditioning
items.plain_en: one event reliably predicting another creates association

items.name: Observational learning
items.plain_en: learning by observing others

items.name: Species specific
items.plain_en: occurs only among same species members

items.name: Modeling
items.plain_en: observation and imitation of behavior

items.name: Latent learning
items.plain_en: hidden learning shown only with reward

items.name: Cognitive map
items.plain_en: mental representation of spatial layout

items.name: Abstract learning
items.plain_en: understanding concepts rather than simple responses

items.name: Insight learning
items.plain_en: sudden realization of problem solution
